newsitem.title: USA: FDA gets new fees, anti-tobacco funds in budget.
newsitem.headline: FDA gets new fees, anti-tobacco funds in budget.

text.p: The Food and Drug Administration would get $34 million to work toward its goal of halving teenage smoking under President Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget proposal released Thursday.
The budget also includes $132 million in new user fees to be paid by the food, health and medical device industries to help pay for more rapid approval of products by the agency.
A similar user fee programme for the prescription drug industry has been popular and is up for renewal, and the budget calls for $91 million, a four percent increase.

The agency would get $24 million for the recently announced food safety programme. Along with other government agencies, the FDA plans to step up measures against E. coli, salmonella and other causes of food-related illnesses.

Fighting teenage smoking has been a high priority of the Clinton administration. Although some of the measures are under attack in court, the FDA hopes to start enacting some new measures against teen smoking later this month.
About one million young people start smoking each year, and the goal is to cut that by 50 percent over seven years.
